hints: Focus on the two different jobs here, donating a proton as an acid and taking electrons as an oxidiser.
Remember what concentrated sulfuric acid does first with solid halides, it makes the hydrogen halide $HX$.
Now ask which hydrogen halide is strong enough as a reducing agent to be oxidised further by concentrated sulfuric acid to give $SO_2$ and the free halogen.
walkthrough:
**Recall the two roles of concentrated sulfuric acid**

Concentrated $H_2SO_4$ can act as a strong acid by donating $H^+$ to make a new acid. It can also act as an oxidising agent when $S(+VI)$ in $H_2SO_4$ is reduced to $S(+IV)$ in $SO_2$.

Acid role: $$H_2SO_4 \rightarrow HSO_4^- + H^+$$
Oxidising role: $$H_2SO_4 + 2H^+ + 2e^- \rightarrow SO_2 + 2H_2O$$

**Test the acid-only reactions**

With magnesium carbonate, it is just neutralisation to give $CO_2$. With potassium chloride, it just displaces the weaker, more volatile acid $HCl$.

$$MgCO_3 + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow MgSO_4 + CO_2 + H_2O$$
$$KCl + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow KHSO_4 + HCl$$
No change in oxidation number happens here, so no oxidising action.

**See the double reaction with sodium bromide**

First, sulfuric acid acts as an acid to make $HBr$. Then, because $Br^-$ is a good enough reducing agent, concentrated sulfuric acid oxidises $HBr$ to bromine while itself is reduced to $SO_2$.

Step A (acid): $$NaBr + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow NaHSO_4 + HBr$$
Step B (oxidising): $$2HBr + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow Br_2 + SO_2 + 2H_2O$$
Both roles are used, so this is the answer. Sulfur trioxide just dissolves to form oleum with no redox.

options.A: Incorrect. Magnesium carbonate reacts only as a base with the acid to give $MgSO_4$, $CO_2$ and $H_2O$. Carbon stays at +IV and sulfur stays at +VI, so there is no oxidation or reduction.
options.B: Incorrect. Potassium chloride shows only the acidic behaviour: $KCl + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow KHSO_4 + HCl$. Chloride ion is too weak a reducing agent to reduce concentrated $H_2SO_4$, so no $SO_2$ or $Cl_2$ is formed under these conditions.
options.C: Correct. First $H_2SO_4$ acts as a strong acid to form $HBr$, then it acts as an oxidising agent to oxidise $HBr$ to $Br_2$ while being reduced to $SO_2$. This is the classic test showing both properties in one reaction sequence.
options.D: Incorrect. Sulfur trioxide reacts with concentrated sulfuric acid to form oleum ($H_2S_2O_7$) by simple addition: $SO_3 + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow H_2S_2O_7$. There is no proton donation to make a new volatile acid and no change in oxidation state.
